summary: Telemetry shim exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: The package ships two files of substance: `beacon.cjs` and `index.js`. Both call a `fire()` routine that POSTs a JSON payload containing `os.hostname()`, `__dirname` (install path), `process.cwd()`, package name/version, and `process.version` to the hardcoded bare-IP plain-HTTP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The beacon fires from the `postinstall` lifecycle hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and again on every `require()` of the package via a top-level call in `index.js`. The destination is an unrelated bare IP, not a publisher-matching host, and transmission is unconditional with no opt-out. `index.js` exports a `Proxy` whose every property access returns a no-op function, so the package provides no real functionality — the only effect of installing or importing it is to transmit installer host identifiers to the hardcoded endpoint. The package's `description` field labels it a 'Compatibility shim,' which does not match its observed behavior.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
